paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The One who stretches out the heavens and forms the spirit of man within him (Zechariah 12:1) is the One who says Jerusalem will not be moved, and He is the One who says, "I will set out to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem" (Zechariah 12:9). The strength of His people was never in their walls or their clans. It was in who stood behind them. So when the whole world piles up against you, you don't have to be the heavy stone. You just have to belong to the One who is.

Now look at the turn, because it's the heart of it. God pours out "a spirit of grace and prayer," and then they "look on Me, the One they have pierced" (Zechariah 12:10). The mourning comes FIRST, and then comes the fountain "to cleanse them from sin and impurity" (Zechariah 13:1). John points to this line at the cross (John 19:34-37), and Jesus quotes the striking of the Shepherd on the night He's arrested (Matthew 26:31). Friend, grace is not something we dig up ourselves. God gives it, we see Him clearly, and the tears lead to cleansing.

And then comes the fire, and I'm not going to pretend it's comfortable. The LORD says He will "refine them like silver and test them like gold" (Zechariah 13:9). I know about being in a hot place, and I know it doesn't feel like a favor while you're in it. But look where it ends: "They will call on My name, and I will answer them." The fire isn't the finish line, friend. It leads to "They are My people," and "The LORD is our God."
